title: Is It Time Yet
trend: TikTok 'It's Time' (videos marking the start of the holiday season timed to the annual mid-November holiday audio; New Engen TikTok list, updated Nov 13 2026, US) + the 'too early for holiday decorations?' debate in mid November — Clint begs to start decorating while Marisol enforces the after-Thanksgiving rule and Gladys, the inflatable snowman in the garage box, pleads to be plugged in; twist: Marisol has secretly been building a winter village in the attic since Halloween because she wants to be the one who says 'it is time'
youtube_title: Middle of November. He wants the lights up. She says it is NOT time yet 🎄
description:
Clint has been waiting all year to start decorating. Marisol says nothing goes up until after Thanksgiving, and Gladys the snowman has been in a box since January. Then the attic starts humming.

#cartoon #animation #funny #holidays #shorts
tiktok_caption: middle of november. he wants the lights up. she says not yet 🎄 #cartoon #animation #funny #holidays

lines.text: Marisol. It is the middle of November. You know what that means.
No.
You were going to say it is time. It is not time.
Hello. I am Gladys. A blow up snowman. In a box in the garage since January.
Is it time? Somebody please tell me it is time.
Gladys says it is time.
Gladys is a bag of air, Clint.
A bag of air with feelings.
Hear me out. Just one string of lights. On the porch.
The rule is after Thanksgiving. That is the rule. Your mother made the rule.
My mother put up her tree in October. She just tells people it is a fall tree.
A fall tree with a star on it. Very sneaky. I respect her.
We are not doing a fall tree.
Fine. No tree. What about one tiny snow globe?
Where is the snow globe, Clint?
In my pocket.
Why is there a snow globe in your pocket?
It is always in my pocket. I shake it when I am sad.
He shook it all through September. It was a hard month.
Okay, new plan. I go outside. I do not decorate. I just stand there. Being festive.
Take me with you. Plug me in. I will stand next to you. Very quietly. Like a neighbor.
A twelve foot snowman is not quiet.
I am nine feet. The other three are confidence.
Marisol. The Hendersons put up their lights yesterday. Blinking ones.
The Hendersons are not my problem.
They have a reindeer that moves its head. It looked at me. It looked right at me.
Okay. I will say this one time. We wait until after Thanksgiving.
That is twelve days.
Twelve days.
Twelve days in a box. I will not survive. I will go flat.
Why are you so against it? You love the holidays.
I do not want to talk about it.
Marisol. What is in the attic?
Nothing is in the attic.
The attic is humming. Attics do not hum.
Is that music? In the attic?
Okay. Fine. Yes. I have been decorating the attic since Halloween.
You what?
A whole winter village. Tiny houses. A tiny train. A tiny skating pond made from a mirror.
I just wanted to be the one who says it, every year. You always say it first.
So say it.
No. It is not time.
Fine. Get the ladder. Get the lights. Get the bag of air.
I am being plugged in. I am filling up. I am so full. I am so happy.
Say it, honey.
It is time.
Eleven months in a box for this. Worth it.
Now we just have to tell my mother about her fall tree.
She knows. She has a winter village too. In her car.
